sources.entry: Cloaker - simple drag-and-drop, password-based file encryption.

summary.one_liner: Cloaker is a simple drag-and-drop desktop app for password-based file encryption and decryption, written in pure Rust with an egui GUI.
summary.what_it_does: Users drop a file onto the window, set a password, and pick an output location to encrypt it; dropping an encrypted file back in, entering the password, and choosing an output location decrypts it. The file format is libsodium-compatible: XChaCha20-Poly1305 secretstream for the data, with the key derived by crypto_pwhash (Argon2id, interactive limits). Since version 5.0 the implementation is pure Rust (dryoc, RustCrypto argon2 and scrypt), so there is no C library to build. Files are interoperable with earlier Cloaker versions and with Cloaker.js, a mobile/web version the author mentions. The README says the tests check every format against libsodium itself. Builds are produced with cargo build --release, and the README describes packaging as a Windows single .exe, a Mac .app bundle, and a Linux AppImage.
use_cases: encrypt a single file with a password
decrypt a file encrypted with Cloaker
simple local file encryption without installing software
exchange files readable by Cloaker.js or earlier Cloaker versions
how_to_run: Run the executable at cloaker/gui/target/release/cloaker (.exe on Windows)
Optional Linux AppImage: see the linuxdeploy steps in the README
notable: Drag-and-drop encryption and decryption with a password, no installation needed on Windows or Mac
Pure Rust implementation since 5.0, replacing the earlier Qt/C++ GUI, with no C library to build
File format interoperable with libsodium, earlier Cloaker versions, and Cloaker.js
Linux AppImage and Mac .app packaging described in the README
caveats: Lost or forgotten passwords mean the data cannot be recovered, per the README's data loss disclaimer
Versions before 4 cannot read files written by 4 or 5
Decrypting files from Cloaker 1.0 or 1.1 requires the filename to end in .cloaker
